summary: Temporary courier escort access: dock-badge expiration mismatch and shipping-label discrepancy for overnight GPU crates
description:
Issue summary:
A third-party courier (Celerex Logistics) is scheduled to pick up two GPU crates (asset tags GPU-1782, GPU-1783) from Redwood's secure warehouse dock at 20:30 on 2026-03-13 (outside normal business hours). The courier was issued a temporary visitor badge token (BadgeToken-CRX-917) via the kiosk, but badge TTL in the building access system expires at 20:00, while dock gate credentials (warehouse shipping system) show a separate allowed window until 22:00. Additionally, the printed shipping labels on the crates do not match the manifest uploaded to the shipping system (manifest references dataset: RDW-RMA-332).

Impact:
- Courier unable to access dock after 20:00 due to building badge TTL, causing potential missed pickup and delayed outbound shipment.
- Security concern: mismatch between physical labels and digital manifest increases risk of asset misrouting.
- Customer-facing SLA risk for an enterprise Dedicated customer awaiting hardware decommission.

Environment:
- Secure warehouse dock, us-west region, building A (on-prem Redwood secure facility).
- Systems involved: facility-access-svc (badge provisioning), dock-gate-controller, warehouse-shipping-app (manifest/labels), Slack #facilities, #security, and #logistics channels.

Requested outcome:
- Extend temporary escort badge TTL to 23:00 for the courier on 2026-03-13 and ensure escort assigned.
- Reconcile physical labels with manifest and reprint corrected labels if required before pickup.
- Document corrective steps and prevent recurrence by aligning badge provisioning TTL with dock window for out-of-hours pickups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule an out-of-hours pickup in warehouse-shipping-app for 20:30 on a weekday.
2) Issue a temporary visitor badge token from facility-access-svc via kiosk or admin panel (TTL defaults to 2 hours, but building policy overrides to nearest business-hour cutoff).
3) Compare TTL shown in facility-access-svc (20:00) with dock-gate-controller allowed window (22:00).
4) Upload manifest to warehouse-shipping-app and print labels; visually inspect label SKU/asset tag vs manifest entries to reproduce mismatch.

comments: Maya Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-13T18:50:00Z: Noticed courier on-site now; issued temp badge token from kiosk, but they reported badge denied at lobby turnstile at 20:05. Escalating to security and facilities.

Security (Ana Rodriguez) - 2026-03-13T19:05:00Z: Lobby access policy enforces building close at 20:00. We can approve escorted entry via manual override if facilities confirms escort. See #security slack thread.

Logistics (Jonas Meyer) - 2026-03-13T19:12:00Z: Confirmed manifest/label mismatch — labels printed from local printer show asset tags GPU-1782/1783 but manifest references GPU-1782/GPU-1829. Suspect localized print spooler cached old manifest.
investigation_notes: Checked facility-access-svc TTL config: default temp badges inherit building business-hours policy (cutoff 20:00). Override requires manager approval or manual backend extension.

Examined warehouse-shipping-app printing subsystem: print job ID 0x9b21 retained an older manifest when the operator re-uploaded a corrected manifest. The print spooler did not flush previous job because driver service (printer-hub) crashed at 16:47 and restarted, replaying a queued job.
Dock-gate-controller supports gate override commands; manual open by security is permitted for escorted transfers when backed by escort ID and pickup manifest verification.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13T20:20Z - Liam Chen (assignee) coordinated with Security Ana Rodriguez to perform a manual entry override at 20:22. Courier was escorted to the dock and pickup completed at 20:50.
2026-03-13T20:35Z - Logistics reprinted corrected labels after clearing print spooler. New labels checksum 0x7ac2 matched manifest; physical labels affixed to crates GPU-1782/GPU-1783.
Root cause: two independent system TTL policies (badge vs dock) plus a print-spooler race condition that left stale labels on the crates.

Immediate fixes: (1) Facilities updated temp badge TTL override runbook to include an expedited override flow for after-hours courier pickups, (2) IT scheduled a patch to printer-hub to flush queued jobs on restart and added a pre-print manifest checksum validation step, (3) Logistics to use on-screen manifest -> print checksum confirmation prior to operator sign-off.
next_steps: 1) Facilities to add a UI toggle for temporary badge TTL extension in facility-access-svc (owner: Liam Chen) — ETA 2026-03-21.
2) IT to deploy a hotfix to printer-hub to flush stale jobs and add checksum pre-print gate (owner: Priya Singh) — ETA 2026-03-18.
3) Logistics to add manifest-vs-label verification step in job checklist and to avoid reusing local print spoolers for high-value shipments (owner: Jonas Meyer) — ETA 2026-03-16.
4) Create a post-incident note in #facilities summarizing the manual override and guidance for escorts.
